title_en: Jinian Street Village Group, Shaba Village, Changzheng Town, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City v. Zunyi Mingshun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over a commercial housing sales contract
ruling_gist_en: When dealing with the performance of a contract under the circumstance of selling one property to two buyers, assessment may be made based on the authenticity of the conclusion of the commercial housing sales contract, the chronological order of signing, the degree of payment, the registration status of the contract, the fact of possession of the disputed real estate, and the status of advance registration.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over commercial housing sales contract; first instance; intermediate people's court; Guizhou Province; legal person; natural person; Contract Law; order of performance of contract for one property sold to two buyers; validity of commercial housing sales contract; determination of fact of possession of house; selling one property to two buyers; commercial housing sale; demolition and resettlement housing; pre-sale filing registration; possession of house; good faith; contract dispute; sales contract; company, etc. commercial housing sales contract dispute
full_text_en:
Jinian Street Villagers' Group, Shaba Village, Changzheng Town, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City v. Zunyi Mingshun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over a contract for the sale of commercial housing

【Ruling Summary】

In addressing the issue of contract performance in cases of "one property sold twice," the evaluation may be conducted from the following aspects: the authenticity of the commercial housing sales contract, the chronological order of signing, the degree of payment, the status of contract filing, the fact of possession of the disputed immovable property, and the status of advance registration.

Plaintiff: Jinian Street Villagers' Group, Shaba Village, Changzheng Town, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City. Domicile: Shaba Village, Changzheng Town, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City, Guizhou Province.
Person in Charge: Zhang Youquan, Head of the Villagers' Group.

Defendant: Zunyi Mingshun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Zunmei Road, Zunyi City, Guizhou Province.
Legal Representative: Chen Daoyuan, Manager of the Company.

Third Parties:
Chu Wenzhen, male, 58 years old, residing in Nan'an City, Fujian Province.
Zeng Zhuzhi, female, 58 years old, residing in Nan'an City, Fujian Province.
Ran Jianhong, male, 61 years old, residing in Meitan County, Guizhou Province.
Fan Yue, female, 59 years old, residing in Meitan County, Guizhou Province.

The plaintiff, Jinian Street Villagers' Group, Shaba Village, Changzheng Town, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City (hereinafter referred to as "Jinian Street Villagers' Group"), filed a lawsuit with the Zunyi Intermediate People's Court of Guizhou Province against the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Zunyi Mingshun Company"), and the third parties, Chu Wenzhen, Zeng Zhuzhi, Ran Jianhong, and Fan Yue, regarding a dispute over a contract for the sale of commercial housing.

Plaintiff's Allegations: In 2005, the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, conducted real estate development within the plaintiff's locality. Besides providing the plaintiff with relocation housing for demolition, the parties also signed a Subscription Agreement on May 29, 2006. By this agreement, the plaintiff subscribed to purchase commercial premises (hereinafter referred to as "storefronts") located at Units 16, 17, and 18 on the first floor, Building C, Jindi Shijia (later renamed Jindi Shijia), Zunmei Road, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City, developed by the defendant. The total construction area was 276.7 square meters, and the total price was RMB 2,125,056. On June 9, 2006, the plaintiff paid a subscription deposit of RMB 600,000, and subsequently paid the full purchase price of RMB 2,125,056 in six installments. The parties formally signed a commercial housing sales contract on November 11, 2008. However, the defendant's actual delivery of the property occurred on April 30, 2007. After taking possession of the property, the plaintiff has continuously occupied and controlled the storefronts, leasing them out and collecting rental income. In December 2012, the defendant sold the aforementioned Units 16 and 17 storefronts to the third parties Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi, and sold Unit 18 storefront to the third party Fan Yue, completing advance sale registration. However, the third parties have not asserted any rights to demand delivery of the storefronts. The plaintiff argues that by selling the storefronts to different specific persons, the defendant's conduct constitutes a "one property sold twice" situation. However, the commercial housing sales contract signed between the plaintiff and the defendant reflects the true intentions of both parties, does not violate mandatory provisions of laws or regulations, and is therefore legally valid. Moreover, the plaintiff has fulfilled the obligation of paying the full purchase price, the defendant delivered the storefronts to the plaintiff on April 30, 2007, and the plaintiff has continuously leased them out since taking possession. This indicates that the defendant had a genuine intention to perform the contract and should continue to perform its contractual obligations to the plaintiff, and the plaintiff is entitled to a priority real right claim over the aforementioned storefronts. Therefore, the plaintiff requests the court to: 1. Confirm that the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" signed by the plaintiff and the defendant on November 11, 2008, is legally valid, order the defendant to continue performing the contract, and confirm that the plaintiff is the owner of Units 16, 17, and 18 on the first floor, Building C, Jindi Shijia, Zunmei Road, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City; 2. Order the defendant and Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi to cancel the advance sale registration procedures for Units 16 and 17 on the first floor, Building C, Jindi Shijia, Zunmei Road, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City; 3. Order the defendant and Ran Jianhong and Fan Yue to cancel the advance sale registration procedures for Unit 18 on the first floor, Building C, Jindi Shijia, Zunmei Road, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City.

Defendant's Defense: The defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, argued that it had initially consulted with the plaintiff, Jinian Street Villagers' Group, to use storefronts 16 through 20 as relocation housing for demolition. Subsequently, this was changed to using storefronts 1 through 7 as relocation housing, while storefronts 16 through 20 were to be purchased by Jinian Street Villagers' Group as commercial housing. However, the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" signed by both parties did not stipulate the method of purchase, payment terms, or other contents, and some clauses were added by the Jinian Street Villagers' Group on its own. Therefore, the contract is invalid. The defendant sold storefronts 16 through 18 to others only because Jinian Street Villagers' Group, after paying only part of the purchase price, was unable to continue and returned the property before it was sold. When the defendant signed the "Provisional Property Delivery Agreement" with Jinian Street Villagers' Group, the storefronts had not yet passed the completion and acceptance inspection. Therefore, the agreement cannot be established. The "Commercial Housing Sales Contracts" signed by the defendant when selling the storefronts to others do not violate any legal provisions, and thus the claims of Jinian Street Villagers' Group cannot be sustained.

Defense of Third Parties Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi: 1. The evidentiary materials submitted by the plaintiff, Jinian Street Villagers' Group, after the expiration of the evidence submission period are neither supplementary evidence nor new evidence and should therefore be excluded. 2. Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi's series of actions—from signing the purchase contract, completing the filing registration, taking possession of the storefronts, signing a lease contract, to mortgaging the property—were all conducted in a reasonable and lawful manner. In contrast, the basis on which Jinian Street Villagers' Group claims "lawful possession" of the storefronts is merely the "Provisional Property Delivery Agreement" signed with the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company. However, Zunyi Mingshun Company does not recognize the legality of this agreement. Based on the evidence presented at trial, this agreement is an invalid contract that violates mandatory legal provisions, and Jinian Street Villagers' Group has not lawfully taken possession of the storefronts. More importantly, even if their "possession" was based on this agreement, it terminated in May 2014. After that, Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi, relying on the purchase contract and the filing registration, entered into a lease contract with an unrelated third party, Su Chuncheng, and collected the rental income. Furthermore, after the trial concluded, on September 3, Jinian Street Villagers' Group illegally seized storefronts 16 and 17. Their purpose was clearly to mislead the court into believing they were still in possession of the property, despite knowing they were no longer in possession. 3. Determining the ownership of immovable property rights should be assessed based on the time of contract formation, the status of payment, the status of property registration, and the status of possession and control. Regarding the time of signing, the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" between Jinian Street Villagers' Group and Zunyi Mingshun Company, signed on November 11, 2008, contains defects, whereas the contract signed between Chu Wenzhen, Zeng Zhuzhi, and Zunyi Mingshun Company is complete and without defects. Regarding payment, Jinian Street Villagers' Group cannot provide evidence of full payment and still owes over RMB 700,000 of the purchase price, whereas Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi have paid all amounts due. Regarding registration, Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi have completed the filing registration for the commercial housing pre-sale, obtaining preliminary recognition from the administrative authorities, whereas Jinian Street Villagers' Group has never submitted any application to the administrative authorities. Regarding possession, Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi have actually occupied and controlled the property since May 2014 and have taken actions such as mortgaging it for loans. In summary, Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi are the lawful owners of Units 16 and 17 and request the dismissal of the claims made by Jinian Street Villagers' Group.

Defense of Third Parties Ran Jianhong and Fan Yue: The plaintiff, Jinian Street Villagers' Group, and the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, added certain content to the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" after it was signed, rendering the contract invalid. Ran Jianhong and Fan Yue signed a "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" with Zunyi Mingshun Company, which issued receipts for the payments received from them. The contract was also filed and registered with the administrative authorities. Therefore, the claims of Jinian Street Villagers' Group cannot be established.

Facts Found by the Zunyi Intermediate People's Court of Guizhou Province:

1.  On December 18, 2005, the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, as the "Demolition Party," entered into a "Demolition Compensation Agreement" with the plaintiff, Jinian Street Villagers' Group, as the "Demolished Party." The agreement concerned "matters related to the demolition of a two-story temporary building constructed within the boundaries of Jinian Street Group, Shaba Village, Changzheng Town," and reached a consensus that Zunyi Mingshun Company would compensate Jinian Street Villagers' Group with 366.8 square meters of commercial storefronts constructed by it. At the end of this agreement, Zunyi Mingshun Company affixed its company seal under Party A, the Shaba Village Villagers' Committee of Honghuagang District, Zunyi City (hereinafter referred to as "Shaba Village Committee") affixed its seal under Party B, and Jinian Street Villagers' Group had its then-head, Gong Xuanqiang, sign his name and affix his personal seal under Party B.

2.  On May 29, 2006, the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, as Party A, and the plaintiff, Jinian Street Villagers' Group, as Party B, signed a "Subscription Agreement." The agreement stipulated that Jinian Street Villagers' Group would purchase from Zunyi Mingshun Company storefronts with an area of 410 square meters and a total price of RMB 3,148,800 (at RMB 7,680 per square meter) located in the "Jindi Shijia" (later renamed "Jindi Shijia") real estate project, Building C, on Zunmei Road, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City, developed by Zunyi Mingshun Company. The parties agreed that Jinian Street Villagers' Group would pay the full amount in three installments: pay a subscription deposit of RMB 600,000 on May 25, 2006; pay RMB 974,400 within one month after Zunyi Mingshun Company obtained the advance sale registration; and pay the remaining balance of RMB 1,574,400 through a loan after signing the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract." At the end of this "Subscription Agreement," Zunyi Mingshun Company affixed its company seal under Party A, Gong Xuanqiang's personal seal was affixed under Party B, and the Shaba Village Committee affixed its seal under the special terms section.

3.  On June 9, 2006, the plaintiff, Jinian Street Villagers' Group, paid the "subscription deposit" of RMB 600,000 to the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, via bank transfer, and Zunyi Mingshun Company issued a "Receipt." On August 22, 2006, Jinian Street Villagers' Group transferred an additional RMB 300,000 as "storefront advance payment" to Zunyi Mingshun Company. On February 12, 2007, Jinian Street Villagers' Group transferred "purchase price" of RMB 100,000 to Zunyi Mingshun Company, which again issued a "Receipt." On June 5, 2007, Jinian Street Villagers' Group lent RMB 200,000 to Zunyi Mingshun Company via transfer, and Zunyi Mingshun Company issued an "IOU." On May 13, 2008, Jinian Street Villagers' Group transferred another "storefront purchase price" of RMB 200,000 to Zunyi Mingshun Company, which issued a "Receipt." On November 11, 2008, Zunyi Mingshun Company issued two "Receipts" to Jinian Street Villagers' Group, one for RMB 594,600 and one for RMB 130,456, both with the reason being "storefront purchase price." Jinian Street Villagers' Group then transferred RMB 130,456 to Zunyi Mingshun Company on November 20, 2008. These two amounts originated from a "Jinian Street Villagers' Group Account Settlement List" prepared after reconciliation between Jinian Street Villagers' Group and Zunyi Mingshun Company, which stated: "2,125,056 - (paid) 1,400,000 - 141,200 - 153,400 - 10,000 - 290,000 = 130,456." This meant: The purchase price was RMB 2,125,056. After deducting RMB 1,400,000 already paid, and deducting the amounts Zunyi Mingshun Company owed to Jinian Street Villagers' Group for land compensation (RMB 141,200), transition fees (RMB 153,400), and a one-time compensation payment (RMB 10,000 plus RMB 290,000, totaling RMB 594,600), the remaining balance was RMB 130,456.

4.  On February 12, 2009, the plaintiff, Jinian Street Villagers' Group, as the buyer, and the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, as the seller, signed a "Commercial Housing Sales Contract." The contract stipulated that Jinian Street Villagers' Group would purchase storefronts 16, 17, and 18 on the first floor, Building C, "Jindi Shijia," developed by Zunyi Mingshun Company, at a price of RMB 7,680 per square meter, with each storefront having a construction area of 73.35 square meters. In this contract, the "Buyer" section, Article 3 "Basic Information of the Commercial Housing Purchased by the Buyer," Article 4 "Pricing Method and Price," Article 17(4) "Right to Name the Residential Community Where the Commercial Housing is Located," Article 19 "Method for Dispute Resolution," and Articles 22 and 24 were filled in with a blue ballpoint pen, while the remaining contents were carbon copies. Article 3 stipulated that the total area of the storefronts purchased by Jinian Street Villagers' Group was 276.7 square meters (73.35 square meters × 3 units + 56.65 square meters for the area exceeding the demolition relocation entitlement), with a total price of RMB 2,125,056. Regarding the handling of property ownership certificates, Article 15 of the contract stipulated: "The seller shall, within 90 days after the commercial housing is delivered for use, submit to the property registration authority the materials required for the seller to provide for the handling of ownership registration..." At the end of the contract, on November 11, 2008, Zunyi Mingshun Company affixed its company seal under "Seller," the Shaba Village Committee affixed its seal under "Buyer," and the former head of Jinian Street Villagers' Group, Gong Xuanqiang, signed his name and affixed his personal seal. On the same day the contract was signed, Zunyi Mingshun Company also issued a "Letter of Commitment" to Jinian Street Villagers' Group, stating: "The business premises (area: 276.7 square meters) of Building C, 'Jindi Shijia,' Outer Ring Road Comprehensive Market, purchased by your unit from our company, and the relocation housing (area: 366.8 square meters)..."

5.  The defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, had already delivered the aforementioned storefronts 1 through 7 and 16 through 18 to the plaintiff, Jinian Street Villagers' Group, for possession and use as early as April 2007. On April 30, 2007, Zunyi Mingshun Company, as Party A, and Jinian Street Villagers' Group, as Party B, signed a "Provisional Property Delivery Agreement," stating: "Party A delivers to Party B for use the following properties: storefronts 1-7, and storefronts 16-20 (half of storefront 20) of Building C, Jindi Shijia. ... (Actual area shall be subject to measurement by the Real Estate Administration Bureau)." Zunyi Mingshun Company affixed its seal at the end of the agreement, and Gong Xuanqiang signed it. On the day of taking possession, Jinian Street Villagers' Group leased storefronts 16 and 17 to "Su Chuncheng" and storefront 18 to "Su Yaoqi" for steel sales. The lease contracts were renewed annually starting from 2011, with rent paid annually.

6.  On June 12, 2007, as measured by the Zunyi Tianluo Real Estate Surveying Office, the total construction area of storefronts 1 through 7 was 423.45 square meters, and the individual construction area of each of storefronts 16 through 18 was 73.35 square meters, totaling 220.05 square meters. On September 6, 2007, Building C of "Jindi Shijia" passed the completion acceptance inspection conducted by the construction, survey, design, development, and supervision units. The Zunyi Municipal Construction Project Quality Supervision Station signed "Approval of Acceptance Opinion" on the "Unit (Division) Project Acceptance Opinion Letter" and affixed its seal on September 10, 2007.

7.  On August 25, 2010, the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, as the seller, and the third party, Chu Wenzhen, as the buyer, signed a "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" for the aforementioned storefronts 16 and 17, at a price of RMB 14,655 per square meter, with each storefront priced at RMB 1,074,944, and a total price of RMB 2,149,888. On December 6, 2012, Chu Wenzhen transferred RMB 1,920,000 to the personal account of "He Caiquan" of Zunyi Mingshun Company via credit union. Zunyi Mingshun Company issued a "Receipt" for the purchase price of RMB 2,150,000 to Chu Wenzhen on the same day. On December 3, 2012, the parties completed the filing registration for the commercial housing pre-sale contract for storefronts 16 and 17 at the Zunyi Real Estate Market Management Office. On May 16, 2013, Zunyi Mingshun Company issued a "Notice of Property Delivery" to Chu Wenzhen, stating: "The business premises, Units 16 and 17, Building C, 'Jindi Shijia,' developed by our company, which you purchased on August 25, 2010, are now ready for delivery. Please take receipt of the property."

8.  On October 25, 2010, the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, as the seller, and the third party, Fan Yue, as the buyer, signed a "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" for the aforementioned storefront 18, at a price of RMB 12,000 per square meter, selling the property to Fan Yue for RMB 880,200. Zunyi Mingshun Company issued a "Receipt" for the purchase price of RMB 880,200 to Fan Yue on the same day. On December 11, 2012, the parties completed the filing registration for the commercial housing pre-sale contract for storefront 18 at the Zunyi Real Estate Market Management Office.

9.  On May 10, 2014, the third party, Chu Wenzhen, entered into a "House Lease Contract" with "Su Chuncheng" (the same person referred to as "Su Chuncheng" earlier), leasing storefronts 16 and 17 to Su Chuncheng, who continued to operate a steel sales business. The lease term was from May 10, 2014, to May 9, 2016. Su Chuncheng paid rent of RMB 82,296 and RMB 100,584 to Chu Wenzhen on May 23, 2014, and May 25, 2015, respectively. On January 15, 2015, Chu Wenzhen and the third party, Zeng Zhuzhi, mortgaged storefronts 16 and 17 to "Zunyi Hengtong Financing Guarantee Co., Ltd." as counter-guarantee property for a bank loan, but the parties did not complete the mortgage registration.

10. On December 24, 2014, the plaintiff, Jinian Street Villagers' Group, sent a rent payment "Notice" to Su Chuncheng's brother, Su Chunquan, informing him that rent had been overdue for 8 months and requiring payment by December 29, 2014. The "Notice" was signed for by "Wang Xiaoming." Su Chunquan, having already paid rent to the third party, Chu Wenzhen, did not pay rent to Jinian Street Villagers' Group and informed Jinian Street Villagers' Group about the lease contract he had signed with Chu Wenzhen.

11. In January 2015, to resolve the ownership dispute over storefronts 16, 17, and 18, the plaintiff, Jinian Street Villagers' Group, filed a lawsuit in the Honghuagang District People's Court of Zunyi City against Zunyi Mingshun Company, Chu Wenzhen, Zeng Zhuzhi, Ran Jianhong, and Fan Yue as defendants. In court, the plaintiff clarified its claims as: 1. Confirm that the "Demolition Compensation Agreement" signed with Zunyi Mingshun Company is valid; 2. Confirm that the "Commercial Housing Sales Contracts" signed by Zunyi Mingshun Company with Chu Wenzhen and Fan Yue, respectively, are invalid; 3. Order Zunyi Mingshun Company to complete the advance registration for storefronts 16, 17, and 18, and to cooperate with Chu Wenzhen, Zeng Zhuzhi, Ran Jianhong, and Fan Yue in facilitating the issuance of the property ownership certificates. After the first-instance trial, Jinian Street Villagers' Group withdrew this lawsuit.

12. On June 8, 2015, the plaintiff, Jinian Street Villagers' Group, sent a "Lawyer's Letter" to Su Chunquan, demanding payment of rent from May 8, 2014 (the expiry date of their lease contract) to June 2015. Su Chunquan again refused, stating that he had already paid rent to the third party, Chu Wenzhen.

13. On July 29, 2015, the plaintiff, Jinian Street Villagers' Group, filed the present lawsuit with the court, requesting the court to: 1. Confirm that the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" signed by the plaintiff and the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, on November 11, 2008, is legally valid, order Zunyi Mingshun Company to continue performing the contract, and confirm that the plaintiff is the owner of Units 16, 17, and 18 on the first floor, Building C, Jindi Shijia, Zunmei Road, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City; 2. Order Zunyi Mingshun Company and the third parties, Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi, to cancel the advance sale registration procedures for Units 16 and 17 on the first floor, Building C, Jindi Shijia, Zunmei Road, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City; 3. Order Zunyi Mingshun Company and the third parties, Ran Jianhong and Fan Yue, to cancel the advance sale registration procedures for Unit 18 on the first floor, Building C, Jindi Shijia, Zunmei Road, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City; 4. Order Zunyi Mingshun Company to bear the litigation costs of this case. Upon inquiry by the court, Jinian Street Villagers' Group clarified that its claim for specific performance of the contract meant "requesting the defendant to handle the property ownership certificate for the plaintiff." After the court's clarification, Jinian Street Villagers' Group voluntarily withdrew its second and third claims, and the court has issued a ruling permitting the withdrawal.

Translation:

During the trial, the following issues were examined: the standing and contractual capacity of the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group. The Jinian Street Villagers Group submitted two "Certificates" issued by the Shaba Village Committee on September 10, 2015, which stated respectively: "The villagers group under the jurisdiction of the Village Committee includes the Jinian Street Villagers Group of Shaba Village, which is established in accordance with the law and possesses independent property... The Jinian Street Villagers Group of Shaba Village still exists." and "Gong Xuanqiang, the former head of the Jinian Street Villagers Group of Shaba Village, signed a demolition compensation agreement, a subscription letter, a provisional handover agreement, and a commercial housing sales contract with Zunyi Mingshun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. on behalf of the villagers group. Since the Jinian Street Villagers Group of Shaba Village does not have an official seal externally, this Village Committee, as the direct manager of the villagers group, accepts the entrustment of the villagers group and affixed its official seal to the agreements signed with Zunyi Mingshun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd." The Changzheng Town People's Government of Honghuagang District, Zunyi City (hereinafter referred to as "Changzheng Town Government") endorsed the two "Certificates" with the comment "verified" and affixed its seal.

Regarding the inconsistency of the shop numbers stipulated in the "Subscription Letter" and the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" signed between the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group, and the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company. Both the Jinian Street Villagers Group and Zunyi Mingshun Company stated that when signing the "Demolition Compensation Agreement" and the "Subscription Letter", it was originally intended to use shops 16-20 as demolition replacement housing and shops 1-7 as subscribed commercial housing. Later, due to insufficient funds of the Jinian Street Villagers Group, the parties negotiated to use shops 1-7 as demolition replacement housing, with the excess area of 56.65 square meters to be compensated by price difference, and shops 16-18 as commercial housing for purchase, and they signed the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract."

Regarding the inconsistency of handwriting in the content of the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" signed between the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group, and the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company. Zunyi Mingshun Company stated that the contract was first filled out by the company and then given to the Jinian Street Villagers Group, so except for the carbon copy content, the remaining terms were added by the Jinian Street Villagers Group themselves. Upon inquiry, although Zunyi Mingshun Company questioned the authenticity and legality of the contract, it did not dispute the content stipulated in Article 3, "Among them, shops 1-7 total 423.45 square meters, of which 366.8 square meters are for replacement housing and 56.65 square meters are purchased by the villagers group," nor the contract unit price of RMB 7,680 per square meter stated in Article 4. Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi did not raise objections to the authenticity of the contract, but they argued that the contractual capacity of the Jinian Street Villagers Group was not appropriate. Ran Jianhong and Fan Yue argued that the contract was invalid because it was filled in after the fact and was not filed with the housing and construction authority.

Regarding the reasons for and the nature of the conduct of the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, in selling shops 16-18 to others. Zunyi Mingshun Company acknowledged that the root cause of the dispute in this case was the company's "dual sale of one property." However, it argued that the reason it sold shops 16-18 to the third parties Chu Wenzhen and Fan Yue was because the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group, was unable to pay the purchase price. Therefore, only after the villagers group returned the shops to the company were they resold. The Jinian Street Villagers Group did not accept this. The court inquired whether the parties had handled the procedures for returning the shops. Zunyi Mingshun Company replied that they had not.

Regarding the payment situation of the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group. As mentioned earlier, the total contract price of RMB 2,125,056 paid by the Jinian Street Villagers Group consisted of seven parts. The defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, argued: The "subscription deposit" of RMB 600,000 paid by the Jinian Street Villagers Group on June 9, 2006; the "shop advance payment" of RMB 300,000 on August 22, 2006; the "house purchase payment" of RMB 100,000 on February 12, 2007; the "shop purchase payment" of RMB 200,000 on May 13, 2008; and the "shop purchase payment" of RMB 130,456 on November 20, 2008, totaling RMB 1,330,456, were payments for the excess area of 56.65 square meters for shops 1-7 and partial payments for shops 16-18. However, the RMB 200,000 paid by the Jinian Street Villagers Group on June 5, 2007, was a loan to the company and could not be offset against the house purchase payment. The RMB 594,600 recorded in the settlement statement were expenses incurred for land compensation, transition compensation, etc., and also could not be offset against the house purchase payment. Therefore, the Jinian Street Villagers Group had not fully paid for shops 16-18. The third parties Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi argued that, firstly, the payments made by the Jinian Street Villagers Group were not for shops 16-18, and secondly, the payment records and the settlement statement were contradictory, so they did not recognize the authenticity of the payments. The third parties Ran Jianhong and Fan Yue agreed with Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi.

Regarding the payment situation of the third parties Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi. Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi stated that their payment method was: RMB 1,920,000 was paid by bank transfer, and the remaining balance was paid in cash. Regarding this, the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group, argued that the RMB 1,920,000 was remitted to "He Caiquan" rather than to the company's account, so the legality of the payment was questionable. The defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, argued that "He Caiquan" was the company's actual controller, and because the company had many debts, the payment was remitted to a personal account, but the company had received the money.

Regarding the payment situation of the third parties Ran Jianhong and Fan Yue. Ran Jianhong stated that he was the actual contractor for Building C of "Jin Di Shi Jia." Because the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, owed him project funds, the parties negotiated to offset part of the project funds with shop 18, and then Fan Yue signed the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" with the company. Zunyi Mingshun Company acknowledged this. The plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group, argued that this sales contract relationship was not genuine and harmed its interests.

Regarding the actual possession and use of shops 16-18. The third parties Chu Wenzhen, Zeng Zhuzhi, Ran Jianhong, and Fan Yue all acknowledged that before May 2014, shops 16-18 were leased out by the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group, which collected the rent. However, after that, Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi claimed that the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, informed Su Chunquan to sign a lease contract with them and pay rent for shops 16 and 17. Ran Jianhong and Fan Yue claimed they also orally notified Su Yaoqi. Zunyi Mingshun Company acknowledged this, while the Jinian Street Villagers Group believed that this conduct could not change the fact that shops 16-18 were in their possession and control. After the trial, on September 3, 2015, the Jinian Street Villagers Group believed that "Su Chunkang's" delayed payment of rent and unauthorized removal from shops 16 and 17 should be considered as a termination of the lease relationship between them. They therefore repossessed shops 16 and 17. Regarding this, Su Chunquan sent a "Request Certificate" to the court, which stated: "...Around May-June 2013, a man claiming to be the boss of the real estate development company brought a middle-aged man to my shop and told me that shops 16 and 17 had been sold to this man named Chu Wenzhen. He said the villagers group was only temporarily managing and renting them out, and told me to sign a contract with Chu Wenzhen. He even showed me Chu Wenzhen's sales contract (and left a photocopy). At that time, I told this boss that I had just signed a contract with the villagers group. The middle-aged man was very angry when he heard that I had signed another contract with the villagers group. The real estate development company boss told me that after this contract term ended, I could not sign with the villagers group again, and the villagers group had no right to sign contracts with me anymore. He said if I didn't want to rent, fine, but if I wanted to rent, I had to sign a contract with Chu Wenzhen... Before the 2014 lease term expired, when the villagers group came to me to renew the contract, I told them again about what the real estate company boss had told me about the shops being sold. I also told them that as a lessee, I would only pay rent to one party, and I couldn't pay rent to both. Moreover, Chu Wenzhen had a proper sales contract. So on May 10, 2014, I signed a two-year lease contract with Chu Wenzhen, with rent paid annually. Both rent payments were made in cash at my shop, and Chu Wenzhen gave me receipts... After I signed the contract and paid the rent to Chu Wenzhen, the village people came to me again. I told them that the real estate company had made me sign a contract with Chu Wenzhen, and I had already signed and paid the rent. I said they should take up the issue with the real estate company and Chu Wenzhen... Initially, I rented from the villagers group. Later, since Chu Wenzhen had the sales contract in hand and the villagers group had no basis, I supported Chu Wenzhen and rented the shops from him..." Chu Wenzhen and Zeng Zhuzhi also submitted this "Request Certificate" as evidence to prove their actual possession and control over shops 16 and 17. To verify the authenticity of the content of the "Request Certificate," the court, upon the joint application of the parties, inquired of Su Chunquan. Su Chunquan stated that the "Request Certificate" was written by himself and sent to the court. Shops 16 and 17 were jointly leased by his brother "Su Chunkang" and himself for a steel business. The "Lease Contracts" for the two shops in question were either signed by "Su Chunkang" himself or signed on his behalf by Su Chunquan, and the rent had been paid. Su Chunquan reiterated that in 2013, when Zunyi Mingshun Company and Chu Wenzhen approached him, he had just signed a new one-year lease contract with the Jinian Street Villagers Group and had informed Chu Wenzhen of this. The court also inquired of Su Yaoqi. Su Yaoqi stated that since 2008, she had been signing lease contracts and paying rent to the Jinian Street Villagers Group. Around August or September of this year, Ran Jianhong told her that the house had been sold to him, but did not inform her that he wanted to rent it to her.

The Intermediate People's Court of Zunyi City, Guizhou Province, held at first instance:

The issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" signed between the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group, and the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, is legally valid; 2. Whether Zunyi Mingshun Company should continue to perform its obligation under the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" signed with the Jinian Street Villagers Group to assist in obtaining the property ownership certificates for shops 16-18 in dispute; 3. Whether the claim of the Jinian Street Villagers Group to confirm that it is the owner of shops 16-18 in dispute can be established.

1. Regarding the validity of the contract. From the perspective of the capacity of the signing parties, although the official seal of the Shaba Village Committee was affixed at the end of the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract," the "buyer" field at the beginning of the contract was filled in with the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group. According to the two "Certificates" issued by the Shaba Village Committee and the Changzheng Town Government, the reason the Shaba Village Committee affixed its seal was that the villagers group did not have an official seal. Therefore, the Village Committee's affixing of the seal was merely an act of agency, and the actual contracting party was the Jinian Street Villagers Group. As an unincorporated organization legally established with certain organizational structures and property, the Jinian Street Villagers Group enjoys civil capacity. It has the proper standing to sign the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" with the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company. From the perspective of the signing process, Zunyi Mingshun Company, "in order to expedite the implementation of the Outer Ring Road Comprehensive Market project," signed a "Demolition Compensation Agreement" with the Jinian Street Villagers Group to "demolish the two-story temporary buildings built within the boundary of Jinian Street, Shaba Village, Changzheng Town." Subsequently, after several rounds of negotiation, the parties ultimately decided to use shops 1-7 on the first floor of Building C of "Jin Di Shi Jia," developed by Zunyi Mingshun Company, as demolition replacement housing, and shops 16-18 as purchased commercial housing. Zunyi Mingshun Company pre-filled the general terms of the contract, affixed its company seal, and then handed it over to the Jinian Street Villagers Group for internal consultation before signing and sealing. It can be seen that the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" was carefully signed after the parties reached a consensus on the purchase of the shops, rather than being backdated or signed after the fact. From the perspective of the contract content, although parts of the contract had inconsistent handwriting with other content, on the one hand, the contract was signed at different times, so it is reasonable for the contract content to be gradually perfected. On the other hand, Zunyi Mingshun Company did not dispute the core content of the contract, such as the shop numbers and areas for replacement housing, the area requiring price differential for the excess square footage of the replacement housing, the shop numbers and areas sold as commercial housing, and the unit price and total price. This indicates that the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" represents the true intention of Zunyi Mingshun Company and the Jinian Street Villagers Group. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 32 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which states, "Where parties enter into a contract in written form, the contract is formed when both parties sign or affix their seals," and Article 44, Paragraph 1, which states, "A contract that is lawfully formed becomes effective upon its formation," the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" signed between the Jinian Street Villagers Group and Zunyi Mingshun Company is a lawful and valid contract because the contracting parties had proper standing, the signing process was genuine, the contract terms were complete, the agreed content fully reflected the purchase and sale intentions of both parties, and it did not violate any mandatory provisions of laws or regulations.

2. Regarding the performance of contractual obligations. The dispute in this case arose from the dual sale of one property by the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company. Although Zunyi Mingshun Company argued that the shops 16-18 in dispute were resold only after the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group, had returned them, it did not submit any procedures for the return of the shops to support this claim. This also contradicts the fact that the Jinian Street Villagers Group had been leasing out the shops in dispute for years. Therefore, the court did not accept this defense. In dealing with the question of contract performance in the case of a dual sale of one property, the evaluation can be made based on the authenticity of the commercial housing sales contract, the chronological order of signing, the degree of payment, the contract filing status, the fact of possession of the disputed real estate, the pre-registration status, and the assertion of rights.

First, the authenticity of the contract. In litigation over real estate disputes arising from dual sales, the fact that a contract is genuine and valid is a prerequisite for determining whether each contract can be performed and whether a later concluded contract can prevail over an earlier one. The "Commercial Housing Sales Contracts" signed between the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group, and the third party Chu Wenzhen with the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, were all acknowledged by Zunyi Mingshun Company as sales contracts. This is consistent with the fact that the Jinian Street Villagers Group and Chu Wenzhen paid the purchase price to Zunyi Mingshun Company. Therefore, the court confirmed the authenticity of the "Commercial Housing Sales Contracts" signed between the Jinian Street Villagers Group and Chu Wenzhen with Zunyi Mingshun Company. Regarding the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" signed between the third party Fan Yue and Zunyi Mingshun Company, since both the third party Ran Jianhong and Zunyi Mingshun Company acknowledged that the essence of this contract was a debt-to-asset conversion agreement, and Ran Jianhong did not provide evidence to prove basic facts such as that he was the contractor or actual builder of the shops in dispute or the amount of the project debt owed by Zunyi Mingshun Company, the court did not recognize the authenticity of this "Commercial Housing Sales Contract."

Second, the chronological order of signing. The "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" between the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, and the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group, was formed on February 12, 2009. In contrast, the third parties Chu Wenzhen and Fan Yue signed "Commercial Housing Sales Contracts" with Zunyi Mingshun Company on August 25, 2010, and October 25, 2010, respectively. It can be seen that the Jinian Street Villagers Group purchased the shops first, and Chu Wenzhen and Fan Yue signed their contracts later. Although creditor's rights are equal, the chronological order of formation of the creditor's rights is an important factor in determining the distribution of property rights.

Third, the status of payment. The degree to which a buyer has paid the purchase price reflects the status of their performance of contractual obligations. Buyers who actively perform their contractual obligations should receive more favorable protection. According to the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" signed between the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group, and the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, the Jinian Street Villagers Group was required to pay a total of RMB 2,125,056 for the purchase of shops 16-18 and the price differential for the excess area. It is an undisputed fact that they had remitted RMB 1,330,456 as payment, which Zunyi Mingshun Company also acknowledged during the trial, so the court confirmed this. Although Zunyi Mingshun Company argued that the RMB 200,000 loan they made to the Jinian Street Villagers Group and the compensation amount of RMB 594,600 could not be offset against the purchase price, the "Settlement Statement for the Jinian Street Villagers Group" bearing the company's official seal recorded a payment of RMB 1,400,000. Subtracting the undisputed RMB 1,200,000 paid by bank transfer, the remaining RMB 200,000, in the absence of evidence from Zunyi Mingshun Company that it had been repaid to the Jinian Street Villagers Group, can only be regarded as an agreement between the parties at the final settlement to offset the loan against the purchase price. Similarly, although the RMB 594,600 was compensation in nature, the parties had also agreed to offset it. Accordingly, the court determined that the Jinian Street Villagers Group had paid the full purchase price. According to the two "Commercial Housing Sales Contracts" signed between the third party Chu Wenzhen and Zunyi Mingshun Company, Chu Wenzhen was required to pay a total purchase price of RMB 2,149,888 to Zunyi Mingshun Company. He paid RMB 1,920,000 by bank transfer. For the remaining balance, Chu Wenzhen claimed it was paid in cash, and Zunyi Mingshun Company issued him a "Receipt" for RMB 2,150,000. The Jinian Street Villagers Group and the third parties Ran Jianhong and Fan Yue did not object to the authenticity of the payment. Therefore, the court also confirmed that Chu Wenzhen had fully paid for shops 16 and 17. Regarding the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" signed between Fan Yue and Zunyi Mingshun Company, since no purchase price was actually paid, the court did not confirm it.

Fourth, the status of contract filing and advance notice registration (pre-registration). In this case, none of the plaintiff, the Jinian Street Villagers Group, or the third parties Chu Wenzhen and Fan Yue applied for advance notice registration of the shops in dispute with the administrative authorities. However, Chu Wenzhen and Fan Yue had applied for pre-sale contract filing and registration with the Zunyi Real Estate Market Management Office for their "Commercial Housing Sales Contracts" signed with the defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Company, while the Jinian Street Villagers Group did not apply for filing. According to Article 20, Paragraph 1 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, which states, "Where the parties conclude an agreement for the sale of a house or any other right to immovable property, they may, in accordance with the agreement, apply to the registration authority for advance notice registration to secure the realization of the right in rem. After the advance notice registration, the disposal of the immovable property without the consent of the holder of the advance notice registration right shall not have the effect of a right in rem," only an advance notice registration of an immovable property has quasi-proprietary effect against third parties. Contract filing only indicates that the buyer is preparing to ultimately acquire the right in rem. Therefore, the contract filing by Chu Wenzhen and Fan Yue can only be considered a reference factor in the distribution of property rights.

Fifth, the circumstance of possession. As discussed above, with respect to Shop Nos. 16 and 17, the Plaintiff Memorial Street Village Group and the Third Party Chu Wenzhen have both paid the full purchase price. At present, the Memorial Street Village Group has the evidentiary advantage of having signed the contract first, taken possession first, and used the property first, while Chu Wenzhen's evidentiary advantage lies in the fact that he has registered the *Commercial Housing Sale Contract* for record-filing. In this regard, although the disputed shops did not yet meet the statutory conditions for delivery at the time the Defendant Zunyi Mingshun Company signed the *Interim Handover Agreement* with the Memorial Street Village Group, the shops had passed the completion inspection and acceptance in September 2007. Pursuant to Article 140 of the *Contract Law of the PRC*, which provides that "where the subject matter is already in the possession of the buyer prior to the conclusion of the contract, the time of entry into effect of the contract shall be the time of delivery," the Memorial Street Village Group, at the latest, legally acquired and took possession of Shop Nos. 16 to 18 on February 12, 2009, by signing the *Commercial Housing Sale Contract* with Zunyi Mingshun Company. The Memorial Street Village Group leased Shop Nos. 16 and 17 to Su Chuncheng and Shop No. 18 to Su Yaoqi, forming a lease contract relationship between the parties. With respect to Shop No. 18, Su Yaoqi signed the contract and paid rent to the Memorial Street Village Group from beginning to end, indicating that the Memorial Street Village Group continuously possessed, enjoyed the benefits of, and disposed of Shop No. 18. With respect to Shop Nos. 16 and 17, although Zunyi Mingshun Company issued a *Notice of Property Handover* to Chu Wenzhen on May 16, 2013, because Shop Nos. 16 and 17 had already been delivered to the Memorial Street Village Group earlier, which had taken possession and leased them out, the said *Notice of Property Handover* could not achieve the effect of delivery. Starting from May 2014, although the written *Lease Contract* between Su Chuncheng and the Memorial Street Village Group expired, the de facto lease contract relationship between them was not terminated. The Memorial Street Village Group continued to legally possess, enjoy the benefits of, and dispose of Shop Nos. 16 and 17. Although Su Chuncheng signed a *Housing Lease Contract* with Chu Wenzhen after Chu showed him the *Commercial Housing Sale Contract*, according to the principle of privity of contract, that contract only binds Su Chuncheng and Chu Wenzhen and has no binding effect on the Memorial Street Village Group. Since Su Chuncheng had first leased from the Memorial Street Village Group, even if the lease relationship between them were terminated, Su Chuncheng, as the contractual counterparty, should first return the shops to the Memorial Street Village Group. The fact that Su Chuncheng directly signed a *Housing Lease Contract* with Chu Wenzhen can neither terminate the lease contract relationship between Su Chuncheng and the Memorial Street Village Group nor preclude the Memorial Street Village Group’s actual possession of Shop Nos. 16 and 17. Accordingly, Chu Wenzhen's argument that after signing the lease contract with Su Chuncheng in May 2014, he legally took possession and exercised actual control over Shop Nos. 16 and 17 cannot be established, and the court does not accept it.

Sixth, the circumstance of asserting rights. When it is difficult to resolve the issue of ownership and performance of a contract for a property sold to two buyers through other means, the buyer should actively seek legal remedies through judicial channels. At the end of 2014, after the Plaintiff Memorial Street Village Group failed to collect rent from Su Chuncheng and learned that Su Chuncheng and the Third Party Chu Wenzhen had signed a lease contract, it filed a lawsuit with the Honghuagang District People's Court of Zunyi City in January 2015. After withdrawing that lawsuit, it again filed a lawsuit with the court in July 2015 to assert its rights. In contrast, Chu Wenzhen and the Third Party Fan Yue did not file a lawsuit as plaintiffs requesting Zunyi Mingshun Company to perform its contractual obligation to assist in obtaining the property certificate but only raised, as third parties in this case, the defense that they were lawful possessors of Shop Nos. 16 and 17. In this regard, "possession" is merely a factual state of actual control over a property protected by law; although it has a quasi-real right nature, it is not a real right itself. In a situation where a property is sold to two buyers, a buyer who takes possession of the property based on a sales contract cannot oppose the buyer who ultimately acquires ownership. In other words, even if Chu Wenzhen's aforementioned defense were established, because the *Commercial Housing Sale Contracts* signed by the Memorial Street Village Group, Chu Wenzhen, and Zunyi Mingshun Company are all valid contracts, and now the Memorial Street Village Group is actively seeking judicial relief by requesting Zunyi Mingshun Company to perform its obligation to assist in obtaining the property certificate for the disputed shops, once the property certificate is completed and the Memorial Street Village Group becomes the owner, even if Shop Nos. 16 and 17 are in the possession of Chu Wenzhen, they should still be returned to the Memorial Street Village Group.

Based on the foregoing, the *Commercial Housing Sale Contract* signed between the Plaintiff Memorial Street Village Group and the Defendant Zunyi Mingshun Company is a valid contract. The Memorial Street Village Group obtained the claim right first, fulfilled its own principal contractual obligations as agreed (i.e., paid the full purchase price), and lawfully took possession of the disputed shops. Pursuant to Article 60 of the *Contract Law of the PRC*, which provides that "the parties shall fully perform their respective obligations as agreed," and Article 107, which provides that "if a party fails to perform its contractual obligations, or performs them in a manner inconsistent with the agreement, it shall bear the liability for breach of contract, such as continuing to perform, taking remedial measures, or compensating for losses," Zunyi Mingshun Company shall continue to perform its unfulfilled contractual obligations. That is, in accordance with Article 15 of the *Commercial Housing Sale Contract* signed with the Memorial Street Village Group, and pursuant to the requirements of Article 14, Paragraph 1 of the State Council's *Interim Regulations on Real Estate Registration*, which provides that "the registration of real estate due to sale, creation of a mortgage, etc., shall be applied for jointly by both parties concerned," and Article 16, Paragraph 1, which provides that "an applicant shall submit the following materials and be responsible for the authenticity of the application materials: (1) a registration application; (2) identity certification materials and power of attorney of the applicant and agent; (3) relevant certification materials of the source of real property rights, certification documents of the cause of registration, and the real property certificate; (4) materials on the boundaries, spatial limits, area, etc. of the real estate; (5) explanatory materials on the interests of others; (6) other materials as required by laws, administrative regulations, and the detailed implementing rules of these Regulations," Zunyi Mingshun Company shall proactively cooperate with and actively assist the Memorial Street Village Group to jointly apply to the real estate registration authority for the registration of real property rights for Shop Nos. 16 to 18 and shall submit the materials required to be provided by the seller for the registration of rights. Although the Third Party Chu Wenzhen registered his *Commercial Housing Sale Contract* signed with Zunyi Mingshun Company for record-filing, he signed the contract later, the claim right was created later, and the record-filing act does not have the effect of publicizing real rights or opposing others. In addition, he failed to lawfully take possession of the disputed shops and did not file a lawsuit with the people's court requesting Zunyi Mingshun Company to perform its contractual obligations. Therefore, the court does not accept his defense arguments. Chu Wenzhen and the Third Party Zeng Zhuzhi may separately assert their rights against Zunyi Mingshun Company. The *Commercial Housing Sale Contract* signed between the Third Party Fan Yue and Zunyi Mingshun Company lacks supporting evidence, so its authenticity is in doubt. Even if the contract was actually signed for the purpose of debt repayment by transfer of property, it is an undisputed fact that Fan Yue and the Third Party Ran Jianhong never legally took possession of Shop No. 18 from beginning to end and did not file a lawsuit to assert their contractual rights. Therefore, their defense arguments are also difficult to establish, and the court does not accept them. Ran Jianhong and Fan Yue may separately assert their rights against Zunyi Mingshun Company.

Regarding the issue of confirmation of rights. Pursuant to Article 9, Paragraph 1 of the *Property Law of the PRC*, which provides that "the creation, alteration, transfer, and extinguishment of real rights in immovable property shall take effect upon registration; without registration, they shall not take effect, unless otherwise provided by law," because the ownership registration for the disputed Shop Nos. 16 to 18 has not yet been completed, the Plaintiff Memorial Street Village Group's claim for confirmation that it is the owner of the disputed shops cannot be established, and the court does not support it.

In summary, the Plaintiff Memorial Street Village Group's claim for confirmation that the *Commercial Housing Sale Contract* signed with the Defendant Zunyi Mingshun Company is valid and its request for Zunyi Mingshun Company to continue performing the contract are established and are hereby supported. The Memorial Street Village Group's claim for confirmation that it is the owner of the disputed Shop Nos. 16 to 18 cannot be established and is hereby dismissed. Accordingly, the Zunyi Intermediate People's Court, Guizhou Province, in accordance with Articles 9, 20, and 28 of the *Property Law of the PRC*, Articles 32, 44, 60, 107, and 140 of the *Contract Law of the PRC*, Articles 14 and 16 of the State Council's *Interim Regulations on Real Estate Registration*, and Article 142 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the PRC*, rendered the following judgment on December 22, 2015:

1. The *Commercial Housing Sale Contract* signed on February 12, 2009, between the Plaintiff, the Memorial Street Village Group, Shaba Village, Changzheng Town, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City, and the Defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., is valid.

2. The Defendant, Zunyi Mingshun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., shall, immediately upon the entry into effect of this judgment, cooperate with and assist the Plaintiff, the Memorial Street Village Group, Shaba Village, Changzheng Town, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City, to jointly apply to the relevant real estate registration authority for the registration of real property rights for Shop Nos. 16, 17, and 18 on the first floor of Building C of the "Jindi Shijia" real estate development project located on Zunmei Road, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City, and shall submit the materials required to be provided by the seller for the registration of rights.

3. The remaining claims of the Plaintiff, the Memorial Street Village Group, Shaba Village, Changzheng Town, Honghuagang District, Zunyi City, are dismissed.
